segments: Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
Year 615.
[The year] 615 [of the Arabs], at the age of seventy-five years,
in a place called 'Alqin (Alqin).
And he was carried to Damascus,
and was buried in the sepulchre which he himself had prepared.
For he was very shrewd,
and patient in harboring resentment, and took vengeance after a long time.
And he left these sons:
al-Malik al-Kamil Nasir al-Din Abu'l-Ma'ali, lord of Egypt;
and al-Malik al-Mu'azzam Muzaffar al-Din 'Isa, lord of Damascus and of Jerusalem;
and al-Malik al-Ashraf Sharaf al-Din Musa, lord of Edessa, of Harran, and of Khilat;
and al-Malik al-Muzaffar Shihab al-Din Ghazi, lord of Mayperqat;
and al-Malik al-Hafiz, lord of Qal'at Ja'bar;
and al-Malik al-'Aziz 'Uthman, lord of Baniyas;
and al-Malik al-Salih Isma'il, lord of Bosra;
and al-Malik al-Fa'iz Ya'qub;
and al-Malik al-Amjad 'Abbas;
and al-Malik al-Afdal Qutb al-Din;
and al-Malik al-Qahir Taj al-Din Ishaq.
And in that same year, when Badr al-Din saw
that Muzaffar al-Din, the lord of Erbil, had made a pact with 'Imad al-Din Zangi, the lord of 'Aqr, to lay waste the territory of Mosul and seize the fortresses,
and that submission was of no benefit with them,
nor was he able by himself to withstand their forces if he opposed them,
he sought refuge with al-Malik al-Ashraf, the lord of Mesopotamia and of Khilat,
and promised him that he would be subject to him,
like one of his own nobles.
And al-Ashraf was pleased with this,
and he sent an army to Nisibis,
to go to Badr al-Din whenever he should summon them.
And in the year 616,
616 of the Arabs, 'Imad al-Din Zangi came down from the fortress of 'Imadiyah to the fortress of 'Aqr,
so as to dominate the places in the plain,
for he was already master over these mountainous [places].
And when Badr al-Din heard [this],
he sent an army to guard the country.
Then those nobles and generals took counsel together to go and attack 'Imad al-Din Zangi near 'Aqr,
without informing Badr al-Din.
And they marched all night,
and when the morning of Sunday dawned upon them, at the end of the first month of the Arabs,
they encountered one another beneath the fortress of 'Aqr.
And the army of 'Imad [al-Din] was broken,
'Imad {OCR?},
Ishaq {OCR?}.
